$comment: features.json - the human/UI half of the Visor feature registry.
features.mk is the build half; the two are cross-checked by
tools/check_features.py, which asserts the id sets match exactly.
This file answers the questions a build manifest has to answer but a
config schema cannot: what does this feature DO, which config keys stop
meaning anything without it, which hotkeys disappear, and which host-side
`visor` subcommands become useless or dangerous.
Fields per feature:
summary   one line, shown in `visor features` and install.sh prompts
group     heading the interactive picker files it under; purely for
display, and features are listed within a group in the order
features.mk declares them
detail    the tradeoff, shown in --list-features and Visor Studio
keys      global boot.conf keys that only mean something with it on
entrykeys per-entry keys that only mean something with it on
hotkeys   menu keys the feature owns
cli       `visor` subcommands that require it on the installed build
section   boot.conf.example section header it owns, for [feat:] tagging
size_kb   allocated .text+.rodata+.data of its objects, per arch, at -O2.
Measured, not guessed; re-measure with tools/check_features.py
--sizes after adding sources. Excludes what the linker shares.
arch      architectures it is meaningful on; absent means all
profiles  profiles it may appear in; absent means any.  Outside those
it is forced off even when named in --features, and the
custom picker does not offer it.  Mirrors FEAT_<f>_PROFILES.

gui.summary: The graphical menu: framebuffer, font, icons
gui.detail: The single biggest thing in the image. Dropping it makes the text menu unconditional rather than a fallback, and takes the baked font and the PNG decoder with it. Everything else visual depends on this.

fade.summary: Fades and crossfades between menu states
fade.detail: Cosmetic. Without it transitions are instant cuts.

screensaver.detail: Blanks or dims the menu after an idle timeout. Only matters if a machine sits at the menu for a long time.

blur.summary: Blurred highlight behind the selected entry
blur.detail: Cosmetic. The selection still highlights without it, just without the blur.

clock.detail: Reads the firmware RTC and draws the time on the menu.

pointer.detail: Pointer cursor and click-to-select. Keyboard navigation is core and always works.

editor.detail: Lets anyone at the keyboard edit the kernel command line before booting - which means adding init=/bin/sh. Drop it on machines where physical access should not mean root.
hotkeys: E - edit the selected entry's cmdline

accent.summary: Accent colours sampled from the wallpaper
accent.detail: Extracts a palette from the background image and recolours the menu to match. Costs real space for a purely cosmetic result.

anim.detail: The playback engine only. It needs at least one decoder - anim_gif or anim_mp4 - to have anything to play.

anim_gif.detail: A GIF parser running before the OS is loaded, on a file read from the ESP. Attack surface if that file is not trusted.

anim_mp4.detail: The largest parser in the image: MP4 container, MJPEG frames, and the compact VBG format. Same caveat as anim_gif, more of it.

capture.detail: Writes PNG and GIF files to the ESP from the menu. Useful for bug reports and for showing the thing off; nothing depends on it.
hotkeys: F10 - record an animated GIF of the menu

filebrowse.summary: Browse and boot files from any readable filesystem (B)
filebrowse.detail: Walks every filesystem the firmware can read and boots an arbitrary EFI binary from it. Convenient, and a way around a curated boot menu. Works in text mode too.

audio.summary: Boot sound through the HD Audio controller
audio.detail: Plays a WAV when the menu opens. The HDA controller is x86 chipset hardware, so this is x86-only. It adds a DMA-programming driver to the pre-OS environment.

rbd.detail: A hidden animated sequence with baked-in audio, on a 1-in-50 roll. Roughly 53 KB, nearly all of it the audio sample. Pure fun, zero function. x86-only, because it needs the audio feature. Only ever built into the full profile - you get it by installing full, not by picking it off a list.

recovery.summary: The rescue console (Esc at the menu)
recovery.detail: The text console you reach when the menu is up but something is wrong. Worth keeping on anything you cannot easily reimage.

gptrepair.detail: Detects a damaged GPT and can restore it from the backup header. The one feature here that can make a machine bootable again after the disk is already broken.

snapshots.detail: Finds btrfs snapshots and offers them as alternate boot targets under an entry (V to cycle).
hotkeys: V - cycle deployments and snapshots for the selected entry

bls.detail: Reads /loader/entries/*.conf, the format systemd-boot and kernel-install write. Without it, distro kernel hooks stop producing menu entries.

discover.summary: Find kernels and OSes with no boot.conf
discover.detail: The reason Visor works out of the box. install.sh tells users they can delete boot.conf and let Visor find things, so this is in every profile.

hotplug.summary: Rescan when a USB disk appears at the menu
hotplug.detail: Picks up removable media plugged in after the menu is already drawn.

luks.summary: LUKS passphrase prompt and keyfile handover
luks.detail: Collects the passphrase at the menu and hands it to the initramfs in a cpio keyfile, so you type it once instead of twice. Dropping it does not make an encrypted root unbootable - the initramfs still prompts.

verify.summary: SHA-256 verification of kernels and initrds
verify.detail: Checks an entry's sha256 before booting it. Cheap, and the base that crypto builds on.

crypto.detail: Decrypts AES-encrypted kernels and initrds at boot with a passphrase. Without it the loader physically cannot boot anything `visor encrypt` produced, so the CLI refuses to encrypt against a build that lacks it.

tpm.detail: Measures the kernel, initrd and cmdline into PCRs before handing off, so a TPM-sealed secret can depend on what actually booted. Dropping it silently changes PCR values and can break an existing seal.

selfheal.summary: Repair a broken or reordered UEFI boot entry
selfheal.detail: Notices when firmware has dropped or demoted Visor's NVRAM boot entry and puts it back. Aimed squarely at the laptops that quietly reset BootOrder.

loader_iface.summary: systemd Boot Loader Interface EFI variables
loader_iface.detail: Publishes LoaderInfo, LoaderEntrySelected and friends, so systemd tooling on the booted system can see what loaded it. Also what `bootctl` reads.

rawboot.detail: Boots kernels that have no EFI stub, via the 16-bit/32-bit boot protocol. x86-only. Needed for some very old or unusually built kernels; most modern distro kernels boot fine without it.

minimal.detail: No graphics at all - the text menu becomes the only menu. For servers, tiny ESPs, and anything where you want the smallest thing that boots. Keeps entry discovery and sha256 verification.

standard.summary: The graphical menu and everything most people use
standard.detail: The graphical menu, discovery, security features, and self-heal - without the animation decoders, screen capture, file browser, audio or the easter egg.

hardened.detail: This is about attack surface, not size. No GIF/MP4/MJPEG decoders, no file browser reading arbitrary ESP paths, no in-menu cmdline editor, no audio DMA driver. PNG stays, because a graphical menu without icons is not a menu - so this is a smaller target, not an airtight one.
hardened.recommended_for: machines where physical access should not mean root

ricer.summary: Everything visual, turned all the way up
ricer.detail: Every decoder, the accent engine, screen capture, the file browser and boot audio.
ricer.recommended_for: desktops you want to look at

full.detail: Exactly what Visor built before this system existed, and the default when no profile is chosen. What packagers and CI build. The only profile that carries everything - including the parts that are not offered anywhere else.
full.recommended_for: packagers, CI, anyone who does not want to think about it

custom.detail: An interactive checklist seeded from another profile. Also what --features gives you non-interactively.
